MASS SHOOTINGS

By: Nicky Troll | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Mass Shootings are more common than you think, right here in our backyard.

Unique Selling Point:
- A SOUTH AFRICAN SPIN TO GLOBAL STORY
- EXCITING RIDE-ALONG
- FIRST HAND ACCOUNTS OF GUN HOMICIDES

Summary:
The risk of mass shooting is an everyday reality in some parts of the country.

This is a story about gun-related violence and the scourge of illegal guns in South Africa by using the recent mass shootings in the US to make comparisons and highlight the differences. We take the opportunity to tell a local story about guns, gangs and dead bodies that will rival any horror mass shooting in the first world.

We take our viewers to streets where gun violence is the order of the day in a ride-a-long with local authorities and take them into the underworld and show them just how common illegal weapons are.


Further information:
In SA, mass shootings are not so much at schools and not necessarily as many victims are killed in a single shooting incident – but the instances of mass shootings are shockingly prevalent. Some as recent as last week in the Western Cape – but South Africans have become immune to the cases, we are shocked by global mass shooting incidents, yet we are ignorant to the prevalence of mass shooting in our backyard.

MASS SHOOTING DEFINITION
The Gun Violence Archive defines mass shootings as "four or more people shot and/or killed in a single incident, at the same general time/location not including the shooter."

The driving forces behind these violent act are different. In the States it is very targeted and there is a desire to shock, a desire to draw attention and make a history so to speak. In South Africa, mass shootings are driven by the illegal economy more often than not. And the victims may not be the target, but rather the collateral damage in a struggle for power.

In the States, the issues is firearm controls and legislation – at home, we’re deaing with illicit firearms that are more common than registered guns.

Sadly, the end result is the same – dead bodies pushing up murder rates.

HOW DO WE TELL IT?
RIDE-ALONG WITH THE CAPE TOWN METRO POLICE
We head into the areas most affected by mass shootings with the Metro Police on their regular patrol to get a sense of the extent and impact of gun-related violence and murders. These scenes will build tension and give viewers an immersive take on the issue.

LOCAL VOICES
We speak to a field worker for the Global Initiative for Trans-Organisational Crime (GITOC) who takes into the community. Lindsay lives in these areas, she knows the gangsters and the victims of these shootings. She will give us insight into the community’s experience and help us understand the driving forces. I imagine filming this in the streets of Mannenberg or Khayelitsha.

VICTIMS
I’ll find a family to interview – who’s lost someone in a mass shooting – Lindsay will speak to the fact that this family’s sorrow is not an isolated case – there are hundreds of families like this.

THE FLIP SIDE
We interview a hidden ID gangster about the illegal gun market, how easy it is to get a weapon, and how easy it is to pull the trigger.

**I’m working on securing a scene with a group of local gangsters to show us their guns – the point would be to show how many there are in just a small group and to bring home the fact that none of the guns are registered.

BIGGER PICTURE EXPERT
Mark Shaw is also from the GITOC, he has written books on illegal guns in SA and done extensive research around weapons in the illicit economies at play in South Africa. He is incredibly well spoken and will give a wider perspective on illegal guns and mass shooting in SA, touching on taxi violence and other driving forces behind the phenomenon.

CRUNCHING THE NUMBERS
THE UNITED STATES
There have been at least 213 known mass shootings in the United States in the first five months of 2022, according to the Gun Violence Archive. There were 692 mass shootings in 2021.

SOUTH AFRICA
It’s not quite the same kind of figures – but in the Western Cape alone there’s been 442 mass shootings in a 2.5-year period. Nearly 600 died, and more than 1000 were wounded.

While the US is a much larger country geographically and has a much bigger population – if you break it down to gun-related homicide rate per 100k population South Africa takes the lead over trigger-happy America- the US sits at 4.46 and South Africa sits at almost double that 8.2.

The total number of murders recorded between October and December 2021 increased by 8.9% - that’s 6 859 killed over 91 days – that’s 75 people murdered every day in SA.

According to Gun Free South Africa, the 2018/19 national police crime statistics show that guns are overwhelmingly the weapon most used in South Africa
to kill, injure, threaten and intimidate. This is evident in the fact that:

 41.3 per cent of murders involved the use of a firearm.
 80 per cent of attempted murders involved firearms
 83 per cent of car hijackings involved the use of at least one firearm.
 59 per cent of residential robberies involved the use of firearms.11

Research done in 2017 by the international organization Small Arms Survey estimated that there were 40 million firearms in the possession of civilians across the continent. The organization says that about 5.8 million of these weapons were officially registered – that put a staggering 34 million guns in the illegal category.

Script:


STRUCTURE: MASS SHOOTINGS

UPSOUND – NEWS REPORT (2 seconds)
VO: Globally, Mass Shootings dominate news cycles – multiple people shot and killed in a single attack – it’s a disturbing trend around the world.

But this story is about South Africa – it’s about indiscriminate shootings and illegal guns.

UPSOUND - BANGING ON DOORS - POLICE MAAK OOP! HEY!!
UPSOUND SERGIO - This area is very dangerous here.

LINK: Mass shootings happen more often than you'd like to think. Right here in our own backyard. But often it goes unnoticed.

VO: These murders are driven by organized crime and fuelled by illegal guns.

JORRIE: There’s no play-play today - the guns are out on the street // Be sure that they are going to target you.

VO: Director Jorissen Lee heads up the Cape Town Metro Police’s Specialized Units.

00.50-01.18 (mixed no VO – for NAN)
JORRIE: There's a hell of a lot of illegal firearms in our streets, on our roads // those illegal guns that are causing the, the carnage, the mayhem.

VO: We hit the streets with the team, on a disruptive operation, in some of the city’s most dangerous neighbourhoods. They’re on the hunt for illegal firearms.

UPSOUND / MUSIC - GEARING UP GETTING INTO NYALA, LEE / SERGIO ON RADIO / JUMPING OUT OF VAN - 5 seconds

UPSOUND – “is daar wit in?”

VO: Drugs and guns go together - gangs protecting their merchandise and their turf.

This footage was captured on the city’s CCTV network - it’s a gang related shooting in Manenberg. These incidents are not the exception, its the rule out there.
** CHECK MUSIC
UPSOUND GUN SHOT

LINK: So what the police are not doing what they're doing. Stop and searches. And this is all part of proactive policing because you never know where you're going to find the guns or who you're going to find them from.

VO: Superintendent Sergio Demingo has worked these streets for 20 years.

SERGIO: We had a shooting in this area I think two days ago.
MAC: How often do you guys do this?
SERGIO: The shooting goes on week for week. Sporadic shootings during the day. So you must deploy in this area each and every day.

UPSOUND 1 second driving shot… siren…

LINK: As exhilarating and exciting as this all is, you're still going into the unknown and you don't know what's waiting for you. It's a bad situation, but this is the reality that these cops face every day.

SERGIO: They're not afraid to fight against the police. / I go out in the mornings, I don't know, we're going to return home.

UPSOUND - HEY OPEN - POLICE! (moment of searching)

SERGIO: Okay that is Mandrax tablets, mandrax tablets, this is your tik, you can see they hide it in very unpleasant places where you don't want to scratch.

VO: The night’s searches turned up drugs, knives and an axe - but NO guns.

UPSOUND - banging on door // Maak oop man!

LINK: Sometimes the police don't find anything here. But that doesn't mean nothing is going on here. It just means visible policing is working.

JORRIE: If we don't evolve with our methodologies and with our practices, we're all going to stay behind the ball all the time. We've enhanced and taken on a lot of technology driven policing and try and pre-empt and predict and prevent the shootings and the carnage that's happening and the criminality.

VO: But during the day, with no cops in sight, we asked around and within minutes, we were shown drugs and guns.

GANGSTER: the people that just want to shoot to kill – they don’t worry about money.

VO: These are career gangsters - they live and die by the barrel of a gun.

GANGSTER: The people you see here are just after the killing – they are bloodhunters.

VO: At just 33, the eldest of the two has spent 10 years in prison for attempted murder - he is one of the main guys out here. But there’s no shortage of new recruits.

GANGSTER: We learn on the battlefield. // it’s how we break the ice. // I just make so, there you go – sleep. And if you do it, you see they shoot someone, now, he’s into it. In it, to win it. In it, to win it.
GANGSTER2: And if I shoot to kill, I think nothing of it.

VO: And it doesn’t matter whose blood it is.

LINK: It's late at night, it's dark, it's cold. Yet children are still running around in the streets. They might not be the target, but a stray bullet could easily find them.

VO: When it comes to mass shootings in South Africa - innocent bystanders are the collateral damage pushing up the body count.

Locally, a mass shooting is classified as an incident where three or more people are shot with a firearm.

In July, at least 45 people were shot dead and 33 injured in eight separate incidents across the country. Some of these cases made headlines. But most mass shootings - don’t.

JENNI: They might not be huge in terms of the number of people killed, but they are quite a common occurrence in the country.

VO: Jenni Irish-Qhobosheane is a researcher for the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime.

JENNI: When we're seeing these kinds of mass shootings is a lot more organized than we think. And it is driven by illicit economies.

VO: From criminality to taxi wars, extortion rackets to drug dominated gangsterism – violence is central in these underworld operations.

In the Western Cape alone – there were 442 mass shootings that left 563 people dead and more than 1,000 others wounded in just 2.5 years.

LYNDSAY: It happens daily whether it’s in Ottery, Manenberg or Hanover Park. It happens all over.

VO: Lyndsay Connoly is a fieldworker for the Global Initiative - these stats are a daily reality for the people who live in these areas.

LYNDSAY: Mass shootings can take place at any time.// whoever sitting in a car, there’s a target. There’s a target walking all the time.
MAC: ALL THE TIME

MOMENT OF WALKING SHOT - 1-2 second breath….

MAC: Even as we’re walking now - anything could happen?
LYNDSAY: They're not shooting to hurt, they’re shooting to kill you.
LYNDSAY: It's not like before the guys used to hit each other with belts or that so that this is not knives, it’s fire arms. // these guys are not here to to play. They are here to kill.
MAC: Jeezsh.

VO: With national murder rates peaking at 71 a day in the country - the killing sprees are getting out of hand.

JENNI: If you look at the current murder rate in the country, it has reached levels that we have not seen since the 1990s. So I think that the illicit firearm market isn't responsible for organized crime, but it is certainly contributing to the way in which organized crime is playing itself out in South Africa.

VO: Besides motives, the biggest difference is that the guns used in American Mass Shootings are often legally obtained, whereas in South Africa - the weapons are usually illegal.

JENNI: A key difference for me between here and the States is we have / very good regulations in place. Whether it's implemented effectively is a different story.
MAC: How difficult Or easy is it to get a gun in South. Africa?
JENNI: It's relatively easy. // gang bosses have set themselves up as mid-level firearm dealers. // if you look just at them historically, //only the key people had access to firearms // Now, every single gang member possesses a firearm.

LINK: We live sheltered lives - out here in the Western Cape, things operate a little differently in gang run areas. Here, carrying a gun is almost as common as carrying a pack of smokes in your pocket.

MAC: How many of you are there in this gang?
GANGSTER: There’s about 30, and about 20 guns.
MAC: Do you guys have a gun? Where do you get this one?
GANGSTER2: This gun, we shot people for this gun. If you kill someone, they give you a gun.
MAC: Then you take it.
GANGSTER2: If you shoot two people, then they give us two guns. We are busy shooting people to get guns. We also buy guns.
MAC: How much does it cost to buy a gun?
GANGSTER2: It all depends on the type of gun.
MAC: There’s no licence here
GANGSTER2: No licence//
MAC: All illegal guns?
GANGSTER2: All.

UPSOUND COCKING GUN

VO: Shockingly, but not surprising - there are almost as many illegal guns as there are legally registered firearms, in circulation, in South Africa.

JENNI: A lot of our firearms are coming from our domestic markets and those would be firearms lost or stolen from civilians and firearms lost and stolen from the state. They treat a gun as if it's like, okay, so you better a table or an eraser. You lost a computer. You lost a firearm. It's an asset that they lose.

VO: But sometimes, it’s more sinister when it comes to police weapons making their way into the underworld.

MAC: DO THEY SELL IT OR// how does it work?
GANGSTER: We buy it from them because they don’t get a lot of money from the state.

VO: With so many illicit guns in circulation, bullets fly regularly.

UPSOUND – SHOOTING - 5 SECONDS

LYNDSAY: I mean, in former years the guys used to run away, hide under the bed, lay flat on the floor. Now, as it's different, life has changed so much that people normally just come out. They come out and they get involved. Social media, their phones, they take pics, and it's like a movie.
MAC: They want to see the violence
LYNDSAY: Now they want to see it.
MAC: They become immune to it,
LYNDSAY: They’ve definitely become immune to the violence in the area. I mean, these kids grow from a young age seeing this violence.
MAC: All the time.
LYNDSAY: All the time.

VO: These two boys are 9 and 10 years old. Drugs, guns, gangs and dead bodies are part of their everyday lives.

PRODUCER: Have you seen some of their guns or do they hide it?
KID1: I’ve seen how they hide it.
KID2: I’ve seen how they shoot, yes.
PRODUCER: Do they shoot here?//
KID1: And I stood there on the stairs, then they came close to me and shot and then my ears went zing.
** FLORIS CUT NICKY GASPING OUT
PRODUCER: Have you seen when someone gets shot?
KID2: Yes, yes, yes, yes.
PRODUCER: Where? Here?
KID1: at the shop/
KID2: /the two of us wanted to walk to YouSave and then they shot.
KID2: Then they shot Funny
PRODUCER: Is Funny ok now, is he still alive.
KID1&2: He’s dead

LEAVE A SLIGHTLY LONGER BREAK TO SINK IN

VO: Both these boys have lost family members in gun fights . And while they seem to have become numb to the violence - children are not immune to the pull of gangs either.

LYNDSAY: Your average gang members starts the age of nine
MAC: Nine? As a nine year old gangsta, what do you do?
LYNDSAY: You become a high risk member, you you a part of alerting people - They fast at nine. So they would carry a firearm.
MAC: No, no, you can't tell me. On the nine year old carrying a firearm.
LYNDSAY: Yes.
MAC: Do they get recruited or is this something that happens?
LYNDSAY: They get recruited // Ottery is basically a fatherless generation with their fathers and fathers being killed, their grandparents being killed. At a young age, they get involved in gangsterism.

VO: A trend the gangsters are shamelessly proud of - having young little gangsters is an advantage to them when it comes to evading the police.

GANGSTER: The cops aren’t aware of them. The cops don’t expect that we’ll give it to a small kid – such a big gun on a kid.
GANGSTER2: When we’re done, we give it to them. They will know what to do.
MAC: Is it? When you’re done then…
GANGSTER2: Yah.

VO: Because out here it seems they don’t know what else to do - it’s a vicious cycle feeding on young blood.

MAC: What's going to happen if none of this stops?
LYNDSAY: It's just going to be a forgotten generation. // More dead bodies. Kids getting killed at a younger age. Innocent people being killed. If it doesn't stop, it's either prison or it's going to be the mortuary.

END



 
PROMO 1 – 21 seconds
VO: THEY are some of the most ruthless killers terrorising the Cape Flats

GANGSTER: They don’t worry about money – the people you see here are just after the killing – they are bloodhunters

VO: And they’re using illegal guns to drive up the body count in South Africa’s mass shootings.


PROMO 2 – 21 seconds
VO: Mass shootings often go unnoticed in South Africa. But not in the Cape Flats.

LYNDSAY: They’ve definitely become immune to the violence in the area. //L3M4

VO: Drugs, guns, gangs and dead bodies are a daily reality for children of these gang-run areas.

PRODUCER: Have you seen when someone gets shot?
KID2: Yes, yes, yes, yes.

PROMO 3 – 11 seconds
VO: This is a story about guns, gangs and dead bodies. Mass Shootings are more common than you think, right here in our own backyard - but often go unnoticed.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: - A SOUTH AFRICAN SPIN TO GLOBAL STORY - EXCITING RIDE-ALONG - FIRST HAND ACCOUNTS OF GUN HOMICIDES
metadata.Summary: The risk of mass shooting is an everyday reality in some parts of the country. This is a story about gun-related violence and the scourge of illegal guns in South Africa by using the recent mass shootings in the US to make comparisons and highlight the differences. We take the opportunity to tell a local story about guns, gangs and dead bodies that will rival any horror mass shooting in the first world. We take our viewers to streets where gun violence is the order of the day in a ride-a-long with local authorities and take them into the underworld and show them just how common illegal weapons are.
metadata.Further information: In SA, mass shootings are not so much at schools and not necessarily as many victims are killed in a single shooting incident – but the instances of mass shootings are shockingly prevalent. Some as recent as last week in the Western Cape – but South Africans have become immune to the cases, we are shocked by global mass shooting incidents, yet we are ignorant to the prevalence of mass shooting in our backyard. MASS SHOOTING DEFINITION The Gun Violence Archive defines mass shootings as "four or more people shot and/or killed in a single incident, at the same general time/location not including the shooter." The driving forces behind these violent act are different. In the States it is very targeted and there is a desire to shock, a desire to draw attention and make a history so to speak. In South Africa, mass shootings are driven by the illegal economy more often than not. And the victims may not be the target, but rather the collateral damage in a struggle for power. In the States, the issues is firearm controls and legislation – at home, we’re deaing with illicit firearms that are more common than registered guns. Sadly, the end result is the same – dead bodies pushing up murder rates. HOW DO WE TELL IT? RIDE-ALONG WITH THE CAPE TOWN METRO POLICE We head into the areas most affected by mass shootings with the Metro Police on their regular patrol to get a sense of the extent and impact of gun-related violence and murders. These scenes will build tension and give viewers an immersive take on the issue. LOCAL VOICES We speak to a field worker for the Global Initiative for Trans-Organisational Crime (GITOC) who takes into the community. Lindsay lives in these areas, she knows the gangsters and the victims of these shootings. She will give us insight into the community’s experience and help us understand the driving forces. I imagine filming this in the streets of Mannenberg or Khayelitsha. VICTIMS I’ll find a family to interview – who’s lost someone in a mass shooting – Lindsay will speak to the fact that this family’s sorrow is not an isolated case – there are hundreds of families like this. THE FLIP SIDE We interview a hidden ID gangster about the illegal gun market, how easy it is to get a weapon, and how easy it is to pull the trigger. **I’m working on securing a scene with a group of local gangsters to show us their guns – the point would be to show how many there are in just a small group and to bring home the fact that none of the guns are registered. BIGGER PICTURE EXPERT Mark Shaw is also from the GITOC, he has written books on illegal guns in SA and done extensive research around weapons in the illicit economies at play in South Africa. He is incredibly well spoken and will give a wider perspective on illegal guns and mass shooting in SA, touching on taxi violence and other driving forces behind the phenomenon. CRUNCHING THE NUMBERS THE UNITED STATES There have been at least 213 known mass shootings in the United States in the first five months of 2022, according to the Gun Violence Archive. There were 692 mass shootings in 2021. SOUTH AFRICA It’s not quite the same kind of figures – but in the Western Cape alone there’s been 442 mass shootings in a 2.5-year period. Nearly 600 died, and more than 1000 were wounded. While the US is a much larger country geographically and has a much bigger population – if you break it down to gun-related homicide rate per 100k population South Africa takes the lead over trigger-happy America- the US sits at 4.46 and South Africa sits at almost double that 8.2. The total number of murders recorded between October and December 2021 increased by 8.9% - that’s 6 859 killed over 91 days – that’s 75 people murdered every day in SA. According to Gun Free South Africa, the 2018/19 national police crime statistics show that guns are overwhelmingly the weapon most used in South Africa to kill, injure, threaten and intimidate. This is evident in the fact that:  41.3 per cent of murders involved the use of a firearm.  80 per cent of attempted murders involved firearms  83 per cent of car hijackings involved the use of at least one firearm.  59 per cent of residential robberies involved the use of firearms.11 Research done in 2017 by the international organization Small Arms Survey estimated that there were 40 million firearms in the possession of civilians across the continent. The organization says that about 5.8 million of these weapons were officially registered – that put a staggering 34 million guns in the illegal category.
